prompt:
You are deciding whether a required test-step sequence fits cleanly into an existing
Allied Telesis test script, or whether a new script is needed.

## Required sequence (case AWPTCM-T33233)

1. action: On the DUT with no pluggable installed in the target port, read the port default configuration with 'show interface portX.Y.Z' (or 'show interface portX.Y.Z status').
   verify: Output reports the port's configured speed as 'auto'/'Auto-negotiate' and duplex as 'auto', confirming Auto is the factory default for both speed and duplex on an empty port.

2. action: After a supported pluggable is present in the target port (insertion is physical — see notes), read the port state with 'show interface portX.Y.Z' and 'show system pluggable'.
   verify: Pluggable is detected/recognized, the port link state reads 'up', and speed/duplex show negotiated values consistent with the pluggable's supported rate — proving autonegotiation completed and a link was established.

3. action: Enter configuration mode on the DUT port and explicitly set 'speed auto' and 'duplex auto'; ensure the link partner port is also configured for auto speed and auto duplex.
   verify: 'show running-config interface portX.Y.Z' reflects speed auto and duplex auto on both ends with no config errors.

4. action: With both DUT and partner on Auto/Auto, bring the link up and read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' on the DUT.
   verify: Link state = up; the port reports negotiation mode as Auto AND displays the concrete negotiated speed and duplex (e.g., 1000/full), confirming Auto mode is reported together with the negotiated values.

5. action: For each supported speed S, force the link partner port to fixed 'speed S' / 'duplex full' while leaving the DUT on Auto/Auto; re-check link after each change with 'show interface portX.Y.Z status'.
   verify: For every supported S, DUT link state = up and DUT-reported negotiated speed equals S with matching duplex, confirming Auto-vs-forced-supported combinations establish a link at the partner's forced rate.

6. action: For each supported speed, set both DUT and partner to the same fixed supported speed/duplex, then repeat with both back on Auto/Auto; read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' after each configuration.
   verify: Link state = up in every supported configuration; when both are Auto the negotiated speed equals the highest common supported rate, confirming a working link across all supported configurations.

7. action: Optionally, send bidirectional test traffic across the negotiated link (Scapy transmit, tcpdump capture on partner) for a representative negotiated configuration.
   verify: All transmitted frames are received with no loss and no CRC/error-counter increments in 'show interface portX.Y.Z' counters, proving the auto-negotiated link is genuinely functional (not merely reported up).

8. action: Configure an incompatible pairing: leave DUT on Auto and force the partner to a duplex the DUT cannot match / an unsupported rate (e.g., partner fixed 'duplex half' or a speed the pluggable does not support), then read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status'.
   verify: DUT link state is reported as 'down' (or the link fails to establish / shows a duplex-mismatch condition); no valid negotiated speed+duplex is presented, confirming incompatible settings do not bring the link up.

9. action: With the port set to Auto/Auto, perform a hot-remove of the supported pluggable (physical — see notes) and read 'show interface portX.Y.Z' and 'show system pluggable' plus the event log.
   verify: On removal, link state transitions to 'down', pluggable no longer listed, and a link-down/pluggable-removed log entry is generated — confirming link status updates correctly on removal.

10. action: Hot-insert the supported pluggable back into the Auto/Auto port (physical — see notes) and read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' and the event log.
   verify: Autonegotiation re-runs cleanly, link state returns to 'up' with expected negotiated speed/duplex, and a link-up/pluggable-inserted log entry is generated.

11. action: Where platform/media support it, enable EcoMode (e.g., 'ecofriendly lpi') on the DUT port over an established Auto-negotiated link, then read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' and 'show ecofriendly' over a short soak.
   verify: EcoMode/LPI reports as enabled, link remains 'up' and stable (no flaps / no error-counter increments), and negotiated speed/duplex are unchanged.

12. action: Disable EcoMode ('no ecofriendly lpi') on the same Auto-negotiated port and re-read 'show interface portX.Y.Z status' and 'show ecofriendly'.
   verify: EcoMode/LPI reports as disabled, link remains 'up' and stable with the same negotiated speed/duplex, confirming EcoMode toggling does not disrupt the auto-negotiated link.

## Rules (strict for repeatable output)
- decision "reuse": one selected script already implements the sequence; running/parametrizing it (possibly with minor edits) is enough. Set base_script to its id.
- decision "extend": one selected script is the right chassis (same topology + configure) and new TestCase classes should be added to a copy of it. Set base_script to its id.
- decision "new": no script is a clean chassis; a new script should be composed, reusing fragments. base_script = null.
- per_step maps every sequence n to what covers it: an existing "script_id:TestCase_x" or "" when it needs new code (fill "gap" with what is missing).
- Consider topology compatibility (devices/ports the TestSet inits) — a perfect TestCase in an incompatible topology is "extend"/"new", not "reuse".
